children.text: harakopānalenaiva bhasmībhūyākarot smaraḥ /

children.text: karoti cinmayaṃ hāsyaṃ jihvākaṇṭhādharagrahaḥ /
children.translated_text: producing playful laughter full of consciousness, seizing the tongue, throat, and lip —

children.text: etad daśaprabhedaṃ hi kṣaraṇasya prakīrtitam // MinSd_166 //
children.translated_text: this tenfold division of [acts leading to] emission is proclaimed. // 166 //

children.text: nārīṇāṃ mohanaṃ tāvad yāvan notkaṇṭhitā priyā /
children.translated_text: The enchantment of women [should continue] until the beloved becomes eager;

children.text: anyathā tatsukhocchitir aśītārkakarād iva // MinSd_167 //
children.translated_text: otherwise, the surge of her pleasure [fades] like [warmth from] a cold sun's rays. // 167 //

children.text: śītkāraṃ cātha huṃkāraṃ hasitaṃ ca trapākṣayaḥ /
children.translated_text: Hissing sounds, 'huṃ' sounds, laughter, loss of modesty,

children.text: prasvinnavadanaṃ caiva vikāro 'tha bhagasya ca // MinSd_168 //
children.translated_text: perspiration on the face, and changes in the vulva — // 168 //

children.text: buddhvā caitāni liṅgāni yoṣitāṃ surate budhaḥ /
children.translated_text: having recognized these signs in women during lovemaking, the wise man,

children.text: tayā tulyasukhaṃ vāñchann anurāgaṃ samācaret // MinSd_169 //
children.translated_text: desiring equal pleasure with her, should practice with passion. // 169 //

children.text: puṣpaṃ mālyaṃ suvarṇaṃ ca rājataṃ taruṇīsukham /
children.translated_text: Flowers, garlands, gold, silver, the pleasure of a young woman —

children.text: taruṇīrahite kānte vyarthaṃ deśaviceṣṭitam // MinSd_170 //
children.translated_text: without a young woman, O lover, [all] regional accomplishments are in vain. // 170 //

children.text: daivād yadi kadācid dhi vicchedaḥ kramaśas tadā /
children.translated_text: If by fate, separation occurs gradually,

children.text: daśamīṃ manmathāvasthāṃ prāpnoty eva na saṃśayaḥ // MinSd_171 //
children.translated_text: one certainly reaches the tenth stage of love-sickness, without doubt. // 171 //

children.text: abhilāṣaś cintanaṃ cānusmṛtir guṇakīrtanam /
children.translated_text: Desire, brooding, recollection, praising [the beloved's] virtues,

children.text: unmādo vipralāpaś ca udvego vyādhir aṣṭamaḥ // MinSd_172 //
children.translated_text: madness, delirious talk, agitation, illness as the eighth, // 172 //

children.text: jaratā maraṇaṃ ceti daśāvasthā manobhuvaḥ /
children.translated_text: stupor, and death — these are the ten stages of <s>Manobhava</s> (Love),

children.text: pramadānāṃ narāṇāṃ ca smaronmathitacetasām // MinSd_173 //
children.translated_text: for women and men whose minds are agitated by <s>Smara</s> (passion). // 173 //

children.text: lakṣayitveṅgitaṃ strīṇāṃ hṛdi vijñaḥ pravartate /
children.translated_text: Having perceived the gestures of women, the wise man acts from the heart;

children.text: satyaṃ vallabhatāṃ yāti sumadhyānāṃ ca yoṣitām // MinSd_174 //
children.translated_text: truly he becomes the beloved of slender-waisted women. // 174 //

children.text: vijñaḥ sādhyāṃ yatnasādhyāṃ vacasā caiva sādhayet /
children.translated_text: The wise man should win over a willing woman and one requiring effort through words;

children.text: sādhanaṃ kaṭhinaṃ strīṇāṃ durnirūpyā bhavanti tāḥ // MinSd_175 //
children.translated_text: winning women is difficult — they are hard to fathom. // 175 //

children.text: prākāśīṃ bāhumūlasya kakṣodarakucasya ca /
children.translated_text: Displaying the root of the arm, the armpit, belly, and breasts;

children.text: bālāliṅganamokṣaṃ ca kavarīmocanaṃ tathā // MinSd_176 //
children.translated_text: playfully embracing and releasing, and loosening the braid; // 176 //

children.text: svīyāṅgāvayavasyaiva nirantaravilokanam /
children.translated_text: constantly gazing at one's own limbs;

children.text: aśrupāto 'ṅgulīmardaśleṣmotsargaṃ muhurmuhuḥ // MinSd_177 //
children.translated_text: shedding tears, rubbing fingers, and frequently releasing phlegm [clearing the throat]; // 177 //

children.text: kāntasya rūpasaubhāgyasaṃkrīḍāguṇasampadām /
children.translated_text: praising the lover's beauty, fortune, playfulness, virtues, and excellence;

children.text: saṃkīrtanaṃ mahollāsaḥ svāṅgabhadrāvamardanam // MinSd_178 //
children.translated_text: great delight, and rubbing one's own auspicious body; // 178 //

children.text: śrutivartmāṅgulikṣepaḥ sasmite vadanekṣaṇe /
children.translated_text: casting a finger toward the ear's edge, gazing at [his] face with a smile —

children.text: etāny aphalasādhyāni liṅgāni ca samunnayet // MinSd_179 //
children.translated_text: these signs of a woman attainable without effort should be recognized. // 179 //

children.text: vrīḍayālaṃkṛtā kāntā ūṣmārtā lobhavarjitā /
children.translated_text: The beloved adorned with modesty, afflicted by warmth, free from greed —

children.text: sādhyā liṅgarthavīryas tā asādhyā sā prakīrtitā // MinSd_180 //
children.translated_text: she who [shows] signs of meaning and ardor is the attainable one; she who does not is proclaimed unattainable. // 180 //

children.text: yatnasādhyā sādhuvaktrī dhanahīnā pravāsinī /
children.translated_text: The one attainable with effort speaks well, is without wealth, or is a traveler;

children.text: sādhyeṅgitaviparyastā yatnasādhyā kuṭumbinī // MinSd_181 //
children.translated_text: she whose gestures are opposite to the attainable type — that housewife requires effort. // 181 //

children.text: udyānotsavatīrtheṣu adhvavāṭīvaneṣu ca /
children.translated_text: In gardens, at festivals, at holy places, on roads, in bazaars, in forests,

children.text: aniṣṭayuvatīsaṅge kṣetre pitṛgṛhe tathā // MinSd_182 //
children.translated_text: in the company of undesirable young women, in the field, at her father's house,

children.text: devāgāre kuṭau caiva tathā vāpyādisevane /
children.translated_text: in temples, in huts, while attending wells and the like,

children.text: naṭane gogṛhe caiva tathā bandhugṛhotsave /
children.translated_text: at dance performances, in cowsheds, and at celebrations in the homes of relatives —

children.text: rakṣitavyā sadā nāryaḥ sadbhir ātmaprayatnataḥ // MinSd_183 //
children.translated_text: women should always be guarded by good men through their own effort. // 183 //

children.text: satyapradānair madhurair vacobhiḥ saṃrakṣitavyā taruṇī sadaiva /
children.translated_text: A young woman should always be protected with truthful, generous, and sweet words;

children.text: arakṣitā cāpi kulasya nāśaṃ kuryāddhi vai bāhyajanānurāgāt // MinSd_184 //
children.translated_text: for even an unguarded woman can bring ruin to the family through attachment to outsiders. // 184 //

children.text: agrāmyamaṇḍanaḥ prājñaḥ śuciḥ śrīmāṃś ca gāyanaḥ /
children.translated_text: Not vulgarly adorned, wise, clean, prosperous, fond of singing,

children.text: narmagoṣṭhīpraviṣṭaś ca ṣaḍguṇo nāgaro mataḥ // MinSd_185 //
children.translated_text: skilled in pleasant conversation — a man with these six qualities is considered a <s>nāgara</s> (urbane gallant). // 185 //

children.text: tyāgī vivekī kuśalaḥ kulīnaḥ kalābhivijñaḥ sumatir dhanāḍhyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Generous, discerning, skillful, well-born, learned in the arts, good-minded, wealthy,

children.text: bhavakṣamaḥ sarvasahaḥ sukhī ca śrīmān suśīlaḥ sa hi nāyakaḥ syāt // MinSd_186 //
children.translated_text: capable of [winning] love, all-enduring, happy, prosperous, and virtuous — such indeed is the <s>nāyaka</s> (hero). // 186 //

children.text: rajakī mālinī dhātrī yoginī prativeśinī /
children.translated_text: A washerwoman, a garland-maker, a nurse, a yoginī, a neighbor,

children.text: sakhī gopālikā ceṭī nāpitā vidhavā naṭī // MinSd_187 //
children.translated_text: a female friend, a cowherd woman, a maidservant, a barber woman, a widow, an actress, // 187 //

children.text: sairandhrī kanyakā caiva daivajñā dūtikā matā /
children.translated_text: a <s>sairandhrī</s> (lady's maid), a young girl, and a female astrologer — these are considered [suitable as] go-betweens (<s>dūtikā</s>).

children.text: vicitrābharaṇā dakṣā parijñātapareṅgitā // MinSd_188 //
children.translated_text: Wearing varied ornaments, skillful, knowing the gestures of others; // 188 //

children.text: pravīṇā sthirabhāvā ca pragalbhā dūtikā matā /
children.translated_text: experienced, steadfast, bold — such is the go-between (<s>dūtikā</s>).

children.text: dūtī niyujyate kārye bahubhāṣāvibhūṣitā // MinSd_189 //
children.translated_text: A go-between is employed in the task, adorned with [skill in] many languages. // 189 //

children.text: roṣānurūpakopā yā anunītā ca tuṣyati /
children.translated_text: She who shows anger proportionate to offense and is pleased when conciliated —

children.text: lakṣyate sā bhṛśaṃ nāthaguṇahāryamanojñayā // MinSd_190 //
children.translated_text: she is clearly perceived as one whose mind is won over by the virtues of her lord. // 190 //

children.text: aharahar anurāgā dūtikāṃ preṣya pūrvaṃ sarabhasam upayāti kvāpi saṃketadeśe /
children.translated_text: Day after day, with growing love, having first sent the go-between, she eagerly goes to some meeting place;

children.text: na mīlati khalu yasyā vallabho daivayogān nigadati bharatas tāṃ nāyikāṃ vipralabdhām // MinSd_191 //
children.translated_text: she whose beloved does not appear by fate's decree — <s>Bharata</s> calls that heroine the <s>Vipralabdhā</s> (Deceived One). // 191 //

children.text: yasyā ratiguṇākṛṣṭaḥ patiḥ pārśve na muñcati /
children.translated_text: She whose husband, attracted by the qualities of love, does not leave her side,

children.text: vicitravibhramāsaktā sā syāt svādhīnabhartṛkā // MinSd_192 //
children.translated_text: who is engaged in varied love-play — she is the <s>Svādhīnabhartṛkā</s> (She Whose Husband is Under Her Control). // 192 //

children.text: yā nityaṃ priyavicchede kāntasaundaryaceṣṭite /
children.translated_text: She who, upon separation from her beloved, [contemplates] the beauty and deeds of her lover,

children.text: dhyāyed ekamanā bhūtvā syāt sā virahiṇī matā // MinSd_193 //
children.translated_text: meditates with single-pointed mind — she is regarded as the <s>Virahiṇī</s> (Woman in Separation). // 193 //

children.text: uddāmamanmathaśarajvaravepamānā romāñcakarṇakusumaṃ kuśalaṃ vahantī /
children.translated_text: Trembling with the fever of <s>Manmatha</s>'s (Love's) unbridled arrows, bearing a flower on her hair with goosebumps [as ornament], skillful,

children.text: niḥśaṅkinī vrajati yā priyasaṃgamāya sā nāyikā khalu bhaved abhisāriketi // MinSd_194 //
children.translated_text: she who goes fearlessly to meet her beloved — she indeed is the heroine called <s>Abhisārikā</s> (She Who Goes to a Tryst). // 194 //

children.text: yā nirlajjā kṛtā gāḍhaṃ madena madanena ca /
children.translated_text: She who is made utterly shameless by intoxication and by passion,

children.text: abhiyāti priyaṃ sābhisārikā kathitā budhaiḥ // MinSd_195 //
children.translated_text: who approaches her beloved — she is called <s>Abhisārikā</s> by the wise. // 195 //

children.text: ajñānān na gato yasyāḥ saṃketam ucitapriyaḥ /
children.translated_text: She whose accustomed beloved did not come to the meeting place through ignorance —

children.text: tadanāgamasaṃtaptā khaṇḍitā sā prakīrtitā // MinSd_196 //
children.translated_text: she, tormented by his non-arrival, is proclaimed the <s>Khaṇḍitā</s> (Woman with a Faithless Lover). // 196 //

children.text: nirasto manyunā kāntaḥ samartho hi yayā punaḥ /
children.translated_text: She by whom the capable lover was dismissed in anger, yet who

children.text: avasthitā vinā tena kupitā kathitā budhaiḥ // MinSd_197 //
children.translated_text: remains without him — she is called <s>Kupitā</s> (the Angry One) by the wise. // 197 //

children.text: bhaved vāsakasajjā sā dūtīdvāreṇa nirjane /
children.translated_text: She is the <s>Vāsakasajjā</s> (She Dressed for the Occasion), who through the intermediary of a go-between, in a secluded place,

children.text: niścityāgamanaṃ bhartur dvārekṣaṇaparāyaṇā // MinSd_198 //
children.translated_text: having confirmed her husband's arrival, is intent upon watching the door. // 198 //

children.text: durvāradāruṇamanobhavayogam āpya paryākulākalitamānasamudvahantīm /
children.translated_text: Having attained the irresistible and terrible union with love, bearing a mind bewildered and burdened with pride,

children.text: durvāramanmathaśarajvaravepamānām utkaṇṭhitāṃ vadati tāṃ bharataḥ kavīndraḥ // MinSd_199 //
children.translated_text: trembling with the fever of <s>Manmatha</s>'s (Love's) irresistible arrows — <s>Bharata</s>, the king of poets, calls her the <s>Utkaṇṭhitā</s> (the Longing One). // 199 //

children.text: priyaikavartinī coṣṇā dhāvatyunmādinī tathā /
children.translated_text: Devoted solely to her beloved, passionate, running about in frenzy;

children.text: tatraivāvasthite kānte virahotkaṇṭhitā matā // MinSd_200 //
children.translated_text: even when her lover remains right there — she is regarded as the <s>Virahotkaṇṭhitā</s> (Longing in Separation). // 200 //

children.text: asādhyāyāḥ sukhaṃ siddhiḥ sādhyāyāś cānurañjanam /
children.translated_text: For the unattainable woman, pleasure comes of its own accord; for the attainable one, through courtship;

children.text: svecchayā vardhate samyakkāmaśāstraprayojanam // MinSd_201 //
children.translated_text: the purpose of <s>kāmaśāstra</s> grows properly through one's own will. // 201 //

children.text: atha śuddhaṃ tathāśuddhaṃ samāsāditatatkriyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Now [mantras are of two kinds:] pure and impure; one who has acquired the [proper] rituals for them —

children.text: mantro gurumukhāl labdhaḥ sidhyaty atra na saṃśayaḥ // MinSd_202 //
children.translated_text: a mantra obtained from the guru's mouth surely succeeds — there is no doubt. // 202 //

children.text: tricāmuṇḍe iti padaṃ tataḥ kvanu kvanu smṛtam /
children.translated_text: The words 'tri-cāmuṇḍe', then 'kvanu kvanu' as prescribed,

children.text: tataḥ padaṃ chanu chanu svakīyaṃ vaśam ānayet // MinSd_203 //
children.translated_text: then the words 'chanu chanu' — [this mantra] brings the desired one under control. // 203 //

children.text: sādhyānāma dvitīyāntaṃ dattvā svāheti yojayet /
children.translated_text: Placing the name of the one to be won in the dative case, one should add 'svāhā';

children.text: sāmānyenāmukīnāmajapaṃ kṛtvā vaśaṃ nayet // MinSd_204 //
children.translated_text: in general, having performed silent recitation with [the formula] 'such-and-such woman's name,' one should bring her under control. // 204 //

children.text: hrīṃ svāheti mantreṇa sādhyānāmānvitena ca /
children.translated_text: With the mantra 'hrīṃ svāhā' combined with the name of the one to be won,

children.text: saptābhimantritaṃ puṣpaṃ yaiva gṛhṇāti sā vaśā // MinSd_205 //
children.translated_text: a flower consecrated seven times — whoever accepts it comes under control. // 205 //

children.text: kākajihvālipakṣau ca suvarṇamalam aśru ca /
children.translated_text: Crow's tongue, bee's wings, gold dust, tears,

children.text: raktaṃ rateś ca lepena vaśīkuryur manīṣiṇaḥ // MinSd_206 //
children.translated_text: and blood of love — the wise bring [women] under control by anointing with these. // 206 //

children.text: sambhogajaṃ vacābījaṃ jihvā cārkadalaṃ sitam /
children.translated_text: A seed of <s>vacā</s> (calamus) born from union, a tongue, a white leaf of the sun-plant —

children.text: saṃcūrṇyāñjitanetrāṇāṃ bhāryāpi vaśatāṃ nayet // MinSd_207 //
children.translated_text: having ground [these] to powder and applied as eye-collyrium, even another's wife is brought under control. // 207 //

children.text: haritālaṃ manaḥśilā raktacandanam etat sarvaṃ cūrṇīkṛtya /
children.translated_text: Yellow orpiment, red arsenic, red sandalwood — all this ground to powder;

children.text: puṣpeṇa saha yasyāḥ śirasi dīyate sā paśuvad vaśyā bhavati /
children.translated_text: when placed on the head of any woman with a flower, she becomes submissive like a beast.

children.text: pecakasya hṛdayaṃ kuṅkumena saha sampiṣya tilakaṃ kuryāt tena loko vaśyo bhavati // MinSd_208 //
children.translated_text: Grinding the heart of an owl with saffron and making a forehead-mark — by this, people are brought under control. // 208 //

children.text: aśvagandhā vacā kuṣṭhaṃ balā nāgabalā tathā /
children.translated_text: <s>Aśvagandhā</s> (winter cherry), <s>vacā</s> (calamus), <s>kuṣṭha</s> (costus), <s>balā</s> (country mallow), <s>nāgabalā</s> (sida veronicifolia),

children.text: māhiṣaṃ navanītaṃ ca gajapippalīsaṃyutam // MinSd_209 //
children.translated_text: buffalo butter combined with long pepper, // 209 //

children.text: piṣṭvā teṣāṃ vilepena gāḍhīkaraṇam uttamam /
children.translated_text: ground and applied as ointment — [this is] an excellent means of making [the organ] firm.

children.text: sampiṣṭaṃ chāgamūtreṇa śūkaśimbīsamudbhavam // MinSd_210 //
children.translated_text: Ground with goat's urine, [using the substance] produced from a thorny bean plant, // 210 //

children.text: nūnaṃ tasya pralepena liṅgaṃ lauhopamaṃ bhavet /
children.translated_text: by anointing with that, the phallus surely becomes hard as iron.

children.text: nīlotpalasitāmbhojakesaraṃ madhu śarkarā // MinSd_211 //
children.translated_text: Blue lotus, white lotus stamens, honey, and sugar — // 211 //

children.text: amīṣāṃ nābhilepena ramate kāmukaś ciram /
children.translated_text: by anointing the navel with these, a lover enjoys for a long time.

children.text: kṣīreṇa kamalaṃ piṣṭvā salilaṃ guṭikākṛtam // MinSd_212 //
children.translated_text: Grinding lotus with milk and forming it into a pill, // 212 //

children.text: upasthe nihitaṃ kuryāt prakīrṇam api ca kvacit /
children.translated_text: one should place it in the genitals, or scatter it here and there.

children.text: asthi kṛṣṇabiḍālasya dakṣiṇapārśvasambhavam // MinSd_213 //
children.translated_text: A bone from the right side of a black cat, // 213 //

children.text: baddhaṃ kaṭitaṭe bījaṃ vibandhaṃ kurute dhruvam /
children.translated_text: tied as a seed at the waist — it certainly produces restraint [against premature emission].

children.text: saptaparṇasya bījaṃ hi stambhayec chukram ātmagam // MinSd_214 //
children.translated_text: for the seed of the <s>saptaparṇa</s> (Alstonia scholaris) tree indeed arrests one's own semen. // MinSd 214 //

children.text: sitaśarapuṃṣāmūlaṃ pāradasahitaṃ kare dhṛtvā /
children.translated_text: The root of white <s>śara</s> (Saccharum munja) held in the hand together with mercury,

children.text: karañjabījaṃ madhyasthaṃ samūlaṃ bandhayed bījam // MinSd_215 //
children.translated_text: with a <s>karañja</s> (Pongamia pinnata) seed placed in the middle — one should bind the semen along with its root. // MinSd 215 //

children.text: ketakībhūmilatāsanamūlībandhavipakvaṃ kusumbhatailam /
children.translated_text: Oil of <s>kusumbha</s> (safflower), cooked with the roots of <s>ketakī</s> (Pandanus), earth-creeper (<s>bhūmilatā</s>), and <s>sana</s> (hemp),

children.text: pādatale lepenāvaśyaṃ bījastambhaṃ nayati puṃsām // MinSd_216 //
children.translated_text: when applied to the soles of the feet, it certainly brings about seminal retention (<s>bījastambha</s>) in men. // MinSd 216 //

children.text: māhiṣadadhisahadevītilamadhusitapadmakesaraṃ militam /
children.translated_text: Buffalo curd, <s>sahadevī</s> (Sida rhombifolia), sesame, honey, and white lotus stamens mixed together —

children.text: cūrṇaṃ nābhivilepād vīryastambhaṃ karoty avaśyam // MinSd_217 //
children.translated_text: this powder, when applied to the navel, certainly produces seminal retention (<s>vīryastambha</s>). // MinSd 217 //

children.text: bṛhatkarañjabījasthaṃ pāradaṃ padmaveṣṭitam /
children.translated_text: Mercury placed inside a large <s>karañja</s> seed, wrapped in a lotus [petal],

children.text: mukhe kṣiptam idaṃ bījaṃ stambhayaty eva niścitam // MinSd_218 //
children.translated_text: this seed, when placed in the mouth, certainly arrests [the semen]. // MinSd 218 //

children.text: kuryād ādau paricchedaṃ mardanaṃ ca viśeṣataḥ /
children.translated_text: First one should make a preparation and especially massage [the ingredients];

children.text: saptāhaṃ bhāvayen māṣaṃ nistuṣaṃ vidalaṃ tataḥ // MinSd_219 //
children.translated_text: for seven days one should soak <s>māṣa</s> (black gram), [then make it] dehusked and split. // MinSd 219 //

children.text: nālikerodakenātha punas teṣāṃ ca bhāvanā /
children.translated_text: Then soaking them again with coconut water,

children.text: tatpaścād ghanabhraṣṭaṃ ca bhakṣayet kṣīrasādhitam // MinSd_220 //
children.translated_text: after that one should eat them roasted in ghee and cooked with milk. // MinSd 220 //

body.translated_text: The lover can then enjoy hundreds of thousands of women. // MinSd 221 //

children.text: yas tūpānaham ākuñcya samānena niyojayet /
children.translated_text: He who contracts the <s>upānaha</s> (perineal region) and engages [it] with the <s>samāna</s> (breath),

children.text: pādāṅguṣṭhena bhūmau tāṃ pīḍayet tu samāhitaḥ // MinSd_222 //
children.translated_text: should press the ground with the big toes, being fully concentrated. // MinSd 222 //

children.text: bhakṣayed athavā dagdhaiś campakīkadalīyutam /
children.translated_text: Or he should eat [a preparation of] burnt <s>campakī</s> (Michelia champaca) combined with plantain,

children.text: atyagrabhāgasaṃyuktaḥ punā ṛddhiṃ prayacchati // MinSd_223 //
children.translated_text: joined with the foremost tip, this again bestows potency. // MinSd 223 //

children.text: kallolinīkānanakandarādau duḥkhāśraye cārpitacittavṛttiḥ /
children.translated_text: In riverside forests, caves, and such places that are difficult to reach, with the mind's activity directed there,

children.text: samṛddham ābaddham abhinnadhairyaḥ ślatho 'pi dīrghaṃ ramate rate // MinSd_224 //
children.translated_text: abundantly, firmly, with unbroken courage — even one who is relaxed enjoys love-making for a long time. // MinSd 224 //

children.text: pāradaṃ ṭaṅkanaṃ vyoṣā kākamācī tathā madhu /
children.translated_text: Mercury, borax, <s>vyoṣā</s> (the three pungents: ginger, pepper, long pepper), <s>kākamācī</s> (Solanum nigrum), and honey —

children.text: kṣiptaliṅgaś ciraṃ nārīṃ drāvayed ramaṇaḥ sadā // MinSd_225 //
children.translated_text: the lover, having inserted [his] <s>liṅga</s> (penis) [anointed with this], always makes the woman melt with pleasure for a long time. // MinSd 225 //

children.text: tumbīpatraṃ ca lodhraṃ ca samabhāgena lepayet /
children.translated_text: Gourd leaves and <s>lodhra</s> (Symplocos racemosa) should be applied in equal parts;

children.text: bhagalepapradatte 'smin prasūtāpy akṣatā bhavet // MinSd_226 //
children.translated_text: when this application is given on the <s>bhaga</s>, even a woman who has given birth becomes [tight] as if untouched. // MinSd 226 //

children.text: palāśodumbaraṃ cāpi tailaṃ kusumasambhavam /
children.translated_text: Also, oil of <s>palāśa</s> (Butea monosperma) and <s>udumbara</s> (Ficus glomerata) flowers

children.text: madhunā yonisaṃlepād gāḍhīkaraṇam uttamam // MinSd_227 //
children.translated_text: with honey, when applied to the <s>yoni</s>, is an excellent method of tightening. // MinSd 227 //

children.text: svīyeṣṭadevatāmantro japtaḥ svārtham ahiṃsakaḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>mantra</s> of one's own chosen deity (<s>iṣṭadevatā</s>), chanted for one's own purpose, being non-harmful,

children.text: yathāvibhūtidānaṃ hi brahmacarye ca tiṣṭhati // MinSd_228 //
children.translated_text: along with the gift of sacred ash (<s>vibhūti</s>), and while maintaining <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibacy) — // MinSd 228 //

children.text: kṛtvādau tatra śuddhiṃ tu punaḥ kṣetre śubhekṣaṇe /
children.translated_text: having first performed purification, then in the auspicious field [of the womb],

children.text: sūryodayapradoṣābhyāṃ viśeṣāc ca svayaṃ balī // MinSd_229 //
children.translated_text: especially at sunrise and twilight, being himself strong — // MinSd 229 //

children.text: kṛtvā caikamanā vijño yadi bījaṃ vimuñcati /
children.translated_text: the wise one, having become single-minded, if he releases the seed,

children.text: sūte māsodaye nūnaṃ guṇavantaṃ yaśasvinam // MinSd_230 //
children.translated_text: she certainly gives birth at the rise of the month to a virtuous and illustrious [child]. // MinSd 230 //
